newsitem.title: USA: Northwest Air pilots seek mediation.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Air pilots seek mediation.

text.p: Pilots at Northwest Airlines Corp said they will seek federal mediation in contract talks with the nation's fourth-largest airline.
In a recorded message to its members, the Air Line Pilots Association said it was dissatisified with the progress of labor negotiations.
"We really came to the point where we felt we were spinning our wheels. But mediation is not a bad thing. We're hopeful that a mediator will help move things along," a pilots' union spokesman said.
A spokesman for Northwest Airlines said the talks are proceeding normally and the pilots' request for mediation is "not unexpected or abnormal."
Labor negotiations began in October 1996, when the current contract became amendable, the union said.
In 1993, Northwest's unionized employees agreed to wage concessions in exchange for stock and labor representation on the company's board of directors.
Labor owns about 30 percent of the company.
